subject: Operational availability schedule and credit ceilings for Q3 pilot
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@axiontech.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@axiontech.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Operational availability schedule and credit ceilings for Q3 pilot

Irene —

Thanks for the intro earlier. We're finalizing procurement for a small Q3 pilot (prod traffic) and need to align on a few SLAs before we proceed:

- Standard uptime target you typically offer for a pilot (hosted vs. dedicated).
- Monthly service credit / remedy cap (we need an upper bound for finance).
- Planned maintenance carveouts: typical notice windows and acceptable monthly maintenance minutes.
- Any latency SLOs you can attach (p95/p99 guidance), and whether those are part of the remedy calculus.

Can you attach your standard template and a quick operational matrix that maps uptime bands to credit amounts? If you have a short counterproposal for a capped credit (we prefer a percent-of-bill cap rather than a hard dollar cap) that would help speed approvals.

We're targeting a quick sign-off this week if the cap is finance-friendly.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Senior Procurement Manager
AxionTech

[Attachment: axiontech-procurement-q.docx (DOCX)]

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@axiontech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational availability schedule and credit ceilings for Q3 pilot

Daniel —

Appreciate the clear list. Attached are two files: a draft SLA template (PDF) and an operational matrix (XLSX) that maps uptime bands to monthly remedy percentages. High-level summary below so your finance/legal teams can triage quickly: 

- Hosted API: standard commitment 99.95% monthly availability.
- Dedicated (reserved/pinned capacity): 99.9% monthly availability for shared pools, 99.95% for pinned dedicated deployments (we can pin for the pilot).
- Latency: we publish operational baselines (p95 under 400ms for typical single-region workloads). Latency breaches generally inform ops prioritization but are not always a standalone credit trigger unless tied to availability or specific contractual p95 SLOs.
- Remedy / credit cap: our suggested default remedy is monthly credit up to the lesser of (a) 30% of the monthly invoice or (b) $50,000. This structure gives finance a ceiling while preserving proportionality.
- Planned maintenance: standard 72-hour notice for any per-customer impacting maintenance and a soft monthly maintenance allowance of up to 120 minutes that is not remediated. Anything beyond that flows into the availability calculation.

If you need tighter maintenance windows or a lower remedy cap (e.g., percent-of-bill), we can draft a counterproposal. Attaching the files now.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Partnerships — Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@axiontech.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@axiontech.com>, AxionTech Legal <legal@axiontech.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational availability schedule and credit ceilings for Q3 pilot

Irene —

Thanks for the quick response and the attachments. A few items from us after an initial review (legal and finance flagged these):

1) Dedicated uptime: for a pinned/dedicated pilot we require 99.95% as a minimum contractual level.
2) Remedy cap: 30% / $50k is higher than our procurement team is comfortable with for a pilot. Can you consider a cap of 15% of monthly spend instead? Prefer percent-based for predictability.
3) Planned maintenance: 72 hours notice is workable, but we need maintenance windows locked to an agreed monthly cap (we propose no more than 90 minutes per month unless agreed otherwise).
4) Latency: p95 under 300ms would be ideal for our customer-facing flows. If latency becomes a regression vector, we need a path to quantify impact (we can provide a small set of test queries/traffic pattern samples if that helps).

I'm attaching a short procurement questionnaire with the questions we're likely to escalate to legal. If you can take a pass with Karthik on tightening the dedicated uptime and offering a lower remedy cap (15–20%), we can move to legal redlines quickly.

Thanks,
Daniel

[Quoted text hidden]

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Legal Ops <legal-ops@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational availability schedule and credit ceilings for Q3 pilot

Daniel —

Thanks — appreciate the clear asks. After aligning with product and finance here's a compromise we can sign up to for the pilot: 

- Dedicated (pinned capacity): 99.95% monthly availability (compliant with your requirement).
- Hosted API (shared): contractual baseline 99.9% monthly availability for the pilot; we can commit to operational targets of 99.95% but the contractual baseline remains 99.9% for shared pools.
- Remedy / credit cap: capped at the lesser of (a) 20% of the monthly invoice or (b) $30,000 for the pilot period. We chose a percent-first approach per your preference but reduced the ceiling to address finance concerns.
- Planned maintenance: agreed 72-hour notice, with a firm cap of 90 minutes/month of non-remediated planned downtime. Anything beyond that will be factored into availability for remedy purposes.
- Latency: we will run your test queries during the pilot. Operational target for the pilot will be p95 < 300ms in the pinned Dedicated environment; if we miss this target repeatedly we'll include latency diagnostics and a joint runbook instead of automatic credits for the first month (we want to avoid immediate credit triggers while engineering stabilizes).

Next steps: I've attached a revised SLA (redwood-sla-draft-v2-axiontech.pdf) with the clause edits highlighted and an updated operational matrix. If that looks good, I'll send a DocuSign envelope (link below) to the signers you indicate.
